classification.difficultyReason: Convert units, standardise a rejection threshold, use symmetry and the normal table, then calculate an expected count.

content.prompt: Packets of sugar are filled and labelled as having a weight of 1 kg. The weights of these packets are normally distributed with a mean of 1.01 kg and a standard deviation of 0.01 kg. A packet of sugar is rejected if its weight is lower than 985 g.

children.label: a
children.prompt: What is the probability that a randomly chosen packet of sugar is rejected? Give your answer correct to 4 decimal places.

answer.worked:
Let $X$ be the packet weight in kilograms. The rejection threshold is $985\text{ g}=0.985\text{ kg}$.
$$\begin{align*}z&=\frac{0.985-1.01}{0.01}\\z&=-2.5\end{align*}$$
By symmetry and the standard normal table,
$$\begin{align*}P(X<0.985)&=P(Z<-2.5)\\P(X<0.985)&=1-P(Z\le2.5)\\P(X<0.985)&\approx1-0.9938\\P(X<0.985)&\approx0.0062.\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: From a batch of 1000 packets of sugar, how many packets would you expect to be rejected?

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Expected number rejected}&=np\\\text{Expected number rejected}&\approx1000\times0.0062\\\text{Expected number rejected}&\approx6.2.\end{align*}$$
Expect approximately 6 packets to be rejected.
